diagnosis_summary: Rock maintainers confirmed that a misconfigured workflow with an endless activation loop could quietly stop other background tasks until Rock was restarted. Commit c45c361 bounds each workflow processing pass to 10,000 activity activations, logs the most frequently activated action type, and leaves the workflow in an error state instead of allowing it to monopolize processing. The issue is labeled Fixed in v19.4; verify exact package inclusion because a release-line label is not an exact build attestation.
workaround_summaries: Use a Rock build proven to contain commit c45c361a5b4e487355da20e21b582e135e1b6465. Until upgraded, identify and correct workflows that repeatedly activate the same action; restarting Rock may restore background processing temporarily, but it does not remove the looping workflow.

verification_playbook.goal: Determine whether the instance lacks the workflow activation guard and has bounded evidence of a looping workflow interrupting background processing.
prerequisites: Know the exact installed Rock version.
Have read-only access to workflow exception summaries and aggregate operational metrics.

steps.title: Check build ancestry
steps.instructions: Confirm whether the installed package contains commit c45c361a5b4e487355da20e21b582e135e1b6465, which adds a per-pass workflow activation limit and error logging.
steps.expected_if_affected: The installed build predates the activation guard or has not been independently verified to contain an equivalent fix.
steps.expected_if_unaffected: The installed build contains the fixing commit or an independently verified equivalent implementation.

steps.title: Review bounded workflow and queue signals
steps.instructions: Review aggregate counts for repeated workflow action activations, workflow-processing errors, and delayed background tasks. Do not export workflow values, action arguments, stack traces, users, or request data.
steps.expected_if_affected: The vulnerable build is present and bounded evidence shows one workflow repeatedly activating an action while other background tasks stop progressing.
steps.expected_if_unaffected: No matching signals appear in the bounded window, although absence cannot disprove an intermittent loop on a vulnerable build.

limitations: Do not deliberately create a looping workflow or enqueue synthetic production work to force reproduction.
A restart can clear the immediate processing stall but cannot prove that the responsible workflow was corrected.

context.scope: in-memory bus using StartTaskQueue while a consumer is blocked
exact workflow processing source revision; release-package inclusion remains independently verifiable
